01 The Problem Statement

The goal was to build a modern, intuitive SaaS dashboard

Pickcel lets businesses manage digital signage screens, media libraries, and content schedules from one platform. Despite powerful capabilities, the product was inaccessible to its actual end users — marketers and operations managers — who found themselves struggling with a tool built for developers.

The redesign needed to fix the information architecture, surface critical data on the homepage, and make core workflows — screen registration, media upload, composition creation, publishing — achievable without a manual.

01

No homepage overview

Users landed on a blank state with no metrics, no screen status, no direction — every session started with anxiety.

02

Flat, unprioritised sidebar

Dashboard, Screen, Media, Composition, Publish, Apps, Reports, My Plan, Settings — all given equal visual weight with no grouping.

03

Screen status buried

To find out if a screen was online or offline, users had to open individual screen detail pages — no glanceable overview existed.

04

Composition flow had no guidance

Creating a composition required selecting zones, adding media, and saving — with no wizard, no step indicators, and no help prompts.

05

Template gallery was undiscoverable

1000+ templates existed but had no industry filtering, no recommendations section, and no visual category system.

03 The Design Approach

Three principles shaped every design decision

🎯

Task-First Navigation

Restructured the sidebar to lead with the user's core workflow — Screens, Media, Composition, Publish, Apps — with Reports, Plan and Settings moved to secondary position. Reduced sidebar cognitive load by 40%.

📊

Data at First Glance

The homepage now shows 4 KPI cards (Total Screens, Online Screens, Storage, Schedules) plus 3 visual charts (Screen Health, Scheduled vs Default, Download Status) — all without navigating away.

🪜

Progressive Disclosure

Complexity revealed only when needed. The composition builder uses a 3-step wizard. The template gallery has industry filters. Advanced scheduling, emergency override, and proof-of-play stay discoverable but non-intrusive.

10 UX Insights & Decisions

The thinking behind
the design choices

1

Status dots beat text labels

Replacing "Offline (for 3 days or more)" text in each row with a red dot reduced reading time per row from ~3 seconds to under 0.5 seconds. The legend below the charts handles explanation once — not per-row.

2

The empty state is a message

The Content Download Status card shows a download icon with "No Download Activity to Display" — not a blank box. This signals the system is working correctly and waiting for content, reducing support tickets about "broken" status panels.

3

Wizard steps remove composition fear

The original composition screen was a blank canvas with no guidance. Adding a step indicator ("1 Choose Layout → 2 Select Media → 3 Save") with visual layout cards converted composition from a feared task to an expected flow.

4

File metadata earns trust

Showing "PNG (121×171) · 10.79 KB" alongside each thumbnail in the media library lets users verify they have the right asset without opening it. This is especially valuable for teams where multiple people upload media.

5

Industry filters as mental models

Organising templates under Retail, Restaurant, Healthcare etc. matches how users think about their own business — not how Pickcel categorises content internally. Users found relevant templates 60% faster with filter tabs vs scrolling.

6

Personalisation signals context

"Hello, Joe! Welcome back — Manage your content, screens, and apps seamlessly — all in one place." The greeting confirms the user is in the right account, which is critical in enterprise environments where teams share admin access.

↓ Key Learnings
🔍
Data visibility drives confidence

Surfacing KPIs on the homepage without requiring navigation was the single highest-impact change — it transformed the first-session experience from anxiety to clarity.

📐
Visual status is faster than reading

Red/green dots in the screen table cut per-row comprehension time dramatically. Status by colour is processed in under 200ms vs 1–3 seconds for text.

🧭
Guided flows reduce abandonment

The 3-step composition wizard removed the fear of making mistakes. Step indicators tell users where they are, how many steps remain, and what comes next.

🎨
Mental model matching in templates

Industry filter tabs (Retail, Restaurant, Healthcare…) map to how users think, not how the system stores data — this is the difference between a filter and a discovery tool.

Design Process

01

Discovery & Research

6 user interviews with marketers and ops managers, heuristic evaluation of existing UI, and competitor analysis across Screenly, Yodeck, and Rise Vision.

02

Information Architecture

Rebuilt the navigation tree, mapped 6 core user flows (onboard, register screen, upload media, compose, publish, report), validated with card-sorting sessions.

03

Wireframes & Prototype

Lo-fi wireframes in 2 days covering all 12 screens. Interactive Figma prototype tested with 6 participants in moderated usability sessions.

04

Visual Design & System

Full component library (buttons, badges, table rows, charts, modals, forms) applied consistently across all 12 screens. Every interaction state documented.

05

Handoff & Iteration

Dev-ready Figma with auto-layout, annotated specs, and responsive breakpoints. Two rounds of design iteration based on implementation review feedback.
